candidate.blueprint_locator: Appendix A → Safe and Effective Care Environment → Management of Care → Case Management, PDF page 20 (file page 23): plan individualized care based on need and provide information on discharge procedures to home or community setting.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — individualized discharge planning/caregiver preparation for transition to home
candidate.educational_objective: Select an individualized post-stroke caregiver education plan that combines practical skill-building with psychoeducational support and includes reassessment after discharge as caregiver needs change.

options.A: Use an individualized plan that combines practical skill-building with psychoeducational support and reassess caregiver needs after discharge.
options.B: Provide a standardized written packet focused on stroke facts and defer practical skills training until home services begin.
options.C: Limit teaching to psychoeducation during hospitalization because practical skills are best learned only after discharge.
options.D: Teach only the client unless the caregiver requests training, then provide the same material used for all families.

candidate.rationale: The AHA/ASA stroke rehabilitation guideline recommends caregiver interventions that combine skill building with psychoeducational strategies, are tailored to the individual caregiver's needs, and include postdischarge assessment with interventions adjusted as needs change. Therefore, option A is the best plan. A standardized information-only approach (B), psychoeducation without skill building (C), and client-only or one-size-fits-all caregiver teaching (D) do not match these recommendations.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports individualized stroke caregiver interventions combining skill-building and psychoeducational strategies, plus postdischarge reassessment and tailoring to changing caregiver needs. Currentness was cross-checked against the AHA/ASA 2025 rehabilitation access policy statement and the 2026 acute ischemic stroke guideline, which continue to reference the adult stroke rehabilitation guideline for poststroke rehabilitation practice.
candidate.source_document_title: Guidelines for Adult Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery: A Guideline for Healthcare Professionals From the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association
candidate.source_locator: Transitions in Care and Community Rehabilitation → Ensuring Medical and Rehabilitation Continuity Through the Rehabilitation Process and Into the Community; paragraph summarizing Class I caregiver/dyad intervention recommendations: combine skill building with psychoeducational strategies, tailor interventions to caregiver needs, and perform postdischarge assessments with tailored interventions based on changing needs.
candidate.stem: A nurse is preparing the family caregiver of a client with residual deficits after stroke for discharge home. Which teaching plan best aligns with American Heart Association/American Stroke Association recommendations for caregiver support?
